title: KV/Prefix Cache Telemetry v2 — Metric Specification
author: Logan Wright
body:
## Summary
This page defines the **v2 telemetry spec** for Redwood’s prefix/KV cache instrumentation. The intent is to make cache effectiveness measurable, comparable across deployments (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and safe to operate at scale (cardinality + cost budgets).

This spec covers:
- Metric names, types, units, and definitions (hit/miss/partial)
- Required/allowed tags and tag normalization rules
- Sampling and aggregation rules (metrics vs per-request events)
- Cardinality budgets and enforcement expectations
- Examples and anti-patterns

**Primary consumers:** Runtime, Telemetry/Analytics, SRE, Optimize recommendations.

---

## Goals
1) Produce **trustworthy cache hit-rate** and **savings** metrics (hit_bytes, saved_prefill_ms) with consistent semantics across runtimes.
2) Enable drilldowns by **tenant / route / model / region / deployment mode** without blowing up cardinality.
3) Support a v0 recommendation engine (heuristics) with enough evidence to suggest actions (prefix normalization, routing/pinning, cache policy tuning, model/version alignment).

## Non-goals
- ML-driven recommendation models (out of scope for this sprint)
- Changing the cache algorithm (this is instrumentation + telemetry only)
- Customer-facing UI polish (Console may show a basic feed; UI is not specified here)

---

## Definitions
### Cache layers
We standardize on `cache_layer` values:
- `prefix`: request prefix cache (a.k.a. prompt-prefix cache)
- `kv`: KV-cache reuse between requests (where applicable)

### Request stages
`stage` indicates which part of request execution the cache affected:
- `prefill`: prompt ingestion / prefill pass
- `decode`: token generation loop

### Cache outcomes
v2 introduces a consistent `outcome` taxonomy for lookup attribution:
- `hit`: the cache provided a reusable entry that covered the full cacheable prefix for this request at lookup time.
- `miss`: no reusable entry was found for the cacheable prefix.
- `partial`: a reusable entry was found but it covered only part of the cacheable prefix.

**Important:** `partial` is not a “soft hit”. It must carry **bytes/tokens coverage** so that hit-rate can be computed as either:
- request-weighted (counts `partial` as 1 request in its own bucket), or
- bytes-weighted (preferred for savings and recommendations).

### Cacheable prompt ratio
The **cacheable prompt ratio** answers: “How much of incoming prompt traffic is structurally eligible for reuse?”

We define:
- `cacheable_prompt_tokens`: tokens in the prefix window that is eligible for caching (post normalization and policy constraints).
- `prompt_tokens`: total prompt tokens for the request.

`cacheable_prompt_ratio = sum(cacheable_prompt_tokens) / sum(prompt_tokens)`.

---

## Metric namespace and naming conventions
### Namespace
All metrics MUST be emitted under the following namespace:
- `redwood.inference.cache.v2.*`

### Naming rules
- Use snake_case for the suffix: `lookup_total`, `saved_prefill_ms_total`, etc.
- Counts use `_total` suffix.
- Avoid embedding dimensions in metric names (use tags).
- Units are encoded in the name when helpful (`_ms`, `_bytes`, `_tokens`).

### Emission models
v2 supports two emission models, with different constraints:
1) **Low-cardinality metrics** (always-on, safe): aggregated counters/histograms with restricted tags.
2) **Sampled per-request events** (optional): structured events used for debugging and recommendations, sampled and gated.

---

## Tagging specification
### Required common tags (all v2 cache metrics)
These tags are REQUIRED on all metrics listed in this spec unless explicitly stated otherwise.

| Tag | Type | Description | Allowed values / normalization |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | Compute region | e.g. `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`; must match gateway region taxonomy |
| `deployment_mode` | string | Deployment surface | `hosted`, `dedicated`, `private` |
| `cache_layer` | string | Cache layer | `prefix`, `kv` |
| `cache_policy` | string | Active policy identifier | stable short id, e.g. `default_v2`, `dedicated_strict_v1`; MUST NOT include tenant names |
| `runtime_train` | string | Runtime release train | e.g. `runtime-2025.07` |
| `outcome` | string | Lookup result bucket | `hit`, `miss`, `partial`, `na` (use `na` only where outcome is undefined, e.g. eviction) |

### Optional tags (restricted; see metric-level allowances)
The following tags are allowed only on specific “breakdown-enabled” metrics (see tables below) and/or only after control-plane aggregation.

| Tag | Type | Description | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant` | string | Tenant identifier | MUST be a stable hashed id (e.g. `t_3f92a1b7`). Never raw company name or UUID. |
| `route` | string | Route identifier | Stable hashed id (e.g. `r_9c01d2`). Never raw path or customer-provided label. |
| `model` | string | Model id | Canonical model slug (e.g. `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`). |
| `model_version` | string | Model version | Semver-ish or build id (e.g. `2025-02-10.1`). Must be bounded by allow-list in gateway. |
| `tier` | string | Tenant tier | `free`, `pro`, `enterprise` |
| `sdk` | string | Client SDK family | `python`, `ts`, `go`, `java`, `unknown` |
| `transport` | string | Protocol type | `rest`, `grpc`, `ws` |

### Prohibited tags (MUST NOT appear in metrics)
These are explicitly forbidden due to cardinality, privacy, or cost:
- `request_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`
- raw prompt content or any derived prompt fingerprint that is not explicitly bounded (see “prefix_bucket” below)
- `user_id`, email, IP address, org name
- raw `route_path` or customer-provided route labels
- `prefix_sha` (unbounded) or any full hash of prompt prefix

### Prefix bucketing (events only)
For sampled per-request **events** only (not metrics), it is allowed to include:
- `prefix_bucket`: small bounded category derived from prefix length and normalization group, e.g. `len_0_256:norm_v2`, `len_256_1024:norm_v2`, `len_1024_plus:norm_v2`.

This exists to support recommendations without leaking prompt data or creating unbounded dimensions.

---

## Cardinality and cost budgets (normative)
This page defines budgets; enforcement details are tracked in ADR-027.

### Cardinality tiers
We define two tiers of metrics:

**Tier A (always-on, safe)**
- Allowed tags: required common tags only
- Target max time-series per region: <= 2,000
- Suitable for default dashboards and SRE alerting

**Tier B (breakdown-enabled, guarded)**
- Allowed tags: required tags + bounded subset of optional tags (`tenant`, `route`, `model`, `model_version`, `tier`)
- Must be produced via **control-plane aggregation** with guardrails:
  - allow-listing + top-K selection
  - “other” bucket for tail values
  - hard drops when budgets exceeded
- Target max time-series per region: <= 50,000

### Budget rules (hard requirements)
- Any metric carrying `tenant` or `route` MUST be Tier B.
- Any metric carrying `model_version` MUST be Tier B and must use the gateway allow-list.
- Any runtime-emitted metric with `tenant` or `route` is a spec violation (runtime does not have stable bounded identifiers and cannot enforce budgets).

---

## Metric catalog (v2)

### 1) Lookup and outcome accounting
These metrics count lookup attempts and outcomes. These are the primary inputs for hit-rate.

| Metric name | Type | Unit | Description | Allowed tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.lookup_total` | counter | requests | Count of cache lookups attempted | Tier A |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.lookup_outcome_total` | counter | requests | Count of lookups by `outcome` (`hit`/`miss`/`partial`) | Tier A |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.lookup_latency_ms` | histogram | ms | Time spent in lookup (includes key compute + index lookup; excludes prefill compute) | Tier A |

Notes:
- `lookup_total` SHOULD equal `sum(lookup_outcome_total{outcome in [hit,miss,partial]})` within small error bounds (sampling not allowed here).
- For `lookup_latency_ms`, `outcome` tag MUST be set; this enables comparing hit vs miss lookup cost.

### 2) Coverage and savings (bytes/tokens + time)
These metrics quantify “how much” was reused and approximate savings.

| Metric name | Type | Unit | Description | Allowed tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.hit_bytes_total` | counter | bytes | Bytes of prompt/KV material served from cache | Tier A |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.cacheable_bytes_total` | counter | bytes | Bytes eligible to be served from cache for this request stream | Tier A |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.saved_prefill_ms_total` | counter | ms | Estimated prefill time saved due to cache reuse | Tier A |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.saved_prefill_ms_estimation_quality_total` | counter | events | Quality bucket for the estimate (`good`, `fallback`, `unknown`) encoded via `outcome` tag: set `outcome=na` and use `cache_policy` to represent estimation mode | Tier A |

Computation requirements:
- `hit_bytes_total` MUST be the reused bytes at the cache layer (prefix or KV). If runtime can only estimate in tokens, convert to bytes consistently (see “Token/byte conversion”).
- `cacheable_bytes_total` MUST represent the maximum reusable bytes given the cache policy and normalization for that request.

### 3) Cache operations (insert/evict)
These metrics help validate cache health, churn, and policy correctness.

| Metric name | Type | Unit | Description | Allowed tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.insert_total` | counter | entries | Cache insert operations | Tier A (`outcome=na`) |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.evict_total` | counter | entries | Cache eviction operations | Tier A (`outcome=na`) |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.evict_reason_total` | counter | entries | Evictions by reason | Tier A + additional tag `evict_reason` (bounded allow-list) |

`evict_reason` allow-list:
- `capacity`
- `ttl`
- `policy_change`
- `manual`
- `unknown`

### 4) Prompt volume and cacheability
These metrics power the cacheable prompt ratio view.

| Metric name | Type | Unit | Description | Allowed tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.prompt_tokens_total` | counter | tokens | Total prompt tokens processed | Tier A |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.cacheable_prompt_tokens_total` | counter | tokens | Prompt tokens eligible for caching | Tier A |

### 5) Breakdown metrics (Tier B; control-plane aggregated)
These enable drilldowns for Optimize and Console dashboards, but MUST obey guardrails.

| Metric name | Type | Unit | Description | Allowed tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.lookup_outcome_total_by_tenant` | counter | requests | Lookup outcomes segmented by tenant | Tier B (adds `tenant`, `tier`) |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.lookup_outcome_total_by_route` | counter | requests | Lookup outcomes segmented by route | Tier B (adds `tenant`, `route`) |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.saved_prefill_ms_total_by_route_model` | counter | ms | Prefill savings segmented by route + model | Tier B (adds `tenant`, `route`, `model`, `model_version`) |
| `redwood.inference.cache.v2.cacheable_prompt_tokens_total_by_route_model` | counter | tokens | Cacheable prompt volume segmented by route + model | Tier B (adds `tenant`, `route`, `model`, `model_version`) |

Guardrail requirements:
- For any given `tenant`, the pipeline SHOULD keep only top-K `route` values by `prompt_tokens_total` over the last 24h and bucket the remainder as `route=other`.
- If `model_version` is missing/unknown, set `model_version=unknown` (do not drop the tag entirely).

---

## Sampling rules
### Metrics (Tier A and Tier B)
- Tier A metrics MUST NOT be sampled.
- Tier B metrics are derived from Tier A and gateway/control-plane attribution; do not apply probabilistic sampling. Instead apply deterministic **top-K and bucketing**.

### Per-request cache events (optional)
We support a sampled structured event for debugging and recommendations. This is NOT used for SRE alerting.

Event name:
- `redwood.inference.cache.v2.cache_outcome_event`

Sampling:
- Default: 1% of requests
- Dynamic: may increase to 5% for Dedicated enterprise tenants under active investigation (must be time-bounded and approved by SRE)

Required event fields (conceptual; implementation varies by sink):
- `timestamp`, `region`, `deployment_mode`, `cache_layer`, `cache_policy`, `stage`
- `outcome` (`hit`/`miss`/`partial`)
- `prompt_tokens`, `cacheable_prompt_tokens`
- `hit_bytes`, `cacheable_bytes`
- `saved_prefill_ms` (if available)
- `tenant` (hashed), `route` (hashed), `model`, `model_version`

Allowed additional event fields (bounded):
- `prefix_bucket` (see earlier definition)
- `fragmentation_hint` (bounded enum; see recommendations PRD)

Prohibited even in events:
- raw prompt content
- raw prefix hashes
- any unique request identifiers unless explicitly approved for a time-bounded debug build (not part of v2 spec)

---

## Units, conversions, and edge cases
### Token vs byte accounting
- Prefer bytes for cache coverage (`hit_bytes_total`, `cacheable_bytes_total`) because it is model-agnostic.
- If runtime only has tokens at the instrumentation point, convert using:
  - `bytes = tokens * avg_bytes_per_token`
  - `avg_bytes_per_token` must be a bounded constant selected per tokenizer family and emitted as part of runtime configuration (not as a metric tag).

### Partial-prefill and streaming retries
- For streaming retries or partial-prefill behavior, do not “double count” `prompt_tokens_total`.
- If a request is retried internally, runtime SHOULD attach retry classification to the event (sampled event only) and metrics MUST be recorded only once per externally visible request.

### Outcome assignment rules (normative)
- If `cacheable_bytes == 0`, set `outcome=na` and do not increment `lookup_outcome_total`.
- If `hit_bytes == cacheable_bytes` and `cacheable_bytes > 0`, set `outcome=hit`.
- If `hit_bytes == 0` and `cacheable_bytes > 0`, set `outcome=miss`.
- If `0 < hit_bytes < cacheable_bytes`, set `outcome=partial`.

---

## How to compute dashboards from v2 metrics (examples)
### Example 1: Global hit-rate (requests-weighted)
Compute over a window (e.g. 5m):
- `hit_rate_req = sum(lookup_outcome_total{outcome="hit"}) / sum(lookup_outcome_total{outcome in ["hit","miss","partial"]})`

Notes:
- This is easy to interpret but can overstate effectiveness when partials dominate.

### Example 2: Coverage-weighted hit-rate (preferred)
- `hit_rate_bytes = sum(hit_bytes_total) / sum(cacheable_bytes_total)`

This answers: “What fraction of eligible bytes were served from cache?”

### Example 3: Cacheable prompt ratio
- `cacheable_prompt_ratio = sum(cacheable_prompt_tokens_total) / sum(prompt_tokens_total)`

### Example 4: Saved prefill per 1k prompt tokens
- `saved_prefill_ms_per_1k = 1000 * sum(saved_prefill_ms_total) / sum(prompt_tokens_total)`

---

## Examples (correct instrumentation)
### Example A: Runtime emits Tier A metrics only
- Runtime emits `lookup_outcome_total` with tags: `region`, `deployment_mode`, `cache_layer`, `cache_policy`, `runtime_train`, `outcome`.
- Gateway/control plane later enriches and aggregates into Tier B breakdowns.

### Example B: Control plane breakdown with safe bucketing
- For `lookup_outcome_total_by_route`, pipeline keeps top 200 routes per tenant (by `prompt_tokens_total`) and buckets the rest into `route=other`.

---

## Anti-patterns (do not do this)
1) **Adding `request_id` to metrics**
   - Creates unbounded time-series and will be dropped by the pipeline.

2) **Tagging metrics with raw route paths**
   - Customer paths are unbounded and may contain sensitive data.

3) **Per-model-version metrics from runtime**
   - Runtime cannot enforce allow-lists or top-K, and model versions can churn.

4) **Using a full prompt prefix hash as a tag**
   - Even if hashed, cardinality is still unbounded and functionally equivalent to logging content.

5) **Defining hit-rate as `hits / lookups` without handling partial**
   - Partial coverage is common in real traffic; ignoring it leads to misleading dashboards and noisy alerts.

---

## Migration notes (v1 → v2)
- v2 replaces inconsistent legacy names with the `redwood.inference.cache.v2.*` namespace.
- v2 standardizes `outcome` and introduces `cacheable_*` counters to prevent over/under-counting.
- Dashboards should be migrated to compute hit-rate from v2 outcomes and coverage.

Recommended migration sequence:
1) Ship Tier A metrics behind feature flag.
2) Validate invariants (lookup_total ≈ sum(outcomes), hit_bytes <= cacheable_bytes).
3) Enable Tier B breakdowns with guardrails.
4) Cut dashboards and alerts to v2 sources; keep v1 for one full release train as a fallback.

---

## Ownership and change control
- Spec owner: Logan Wright (Telemetry/Analytics)
- Runtime implementation lead: Omar El-Sayed
- Control-plane attribution lead: Ethan Park
- SRE reviewer: Sean Gallagher

Changes to required tags, outcome semantics, or budgets require:
- Update to this page
- Corresponding ADR update if budgets/guardrails change
- SRE sign-off if alert inputs are impacted
